criteria.reason: The record explicitly denies bowel or bladder changes, fever, weight loss, and history of cancer (VN-3). There is no mention of saddle numbness, new bladder/bowel problems, infection signs, major trauma, unexplained weight loss, or rapidly worsening deficit. Therefore, there is no evidence to support the presence of a red flag.
Symptoms persist after more than two months (approx. 8 weeks) of physical therapy and daily naproxen, which satisfies the six-week requirement.
Patient reports numbness and tingling along the outer left calf, indicating pain or sensory changes in a nerve root pattern.

The record mentions patient-reported numbness and tingling (VN-7) but does not document objective findings such as measurable weakness, reflex loss, or sensory level deficits on examination. No sentence contradicts the possibility of a deficit either.
